title: Part 4
html:
Vateshvara, Munna, Venkata. The robber Pantha Bhil. Girishvara and the silent ascetic. Tripadi, Pana-Narasimha, Vishnukanchi, Pakshitirtha (pp. 61–80)

[p. 61]

658Tirtharam gave up worldly things like a straw,
and, crying "Hari!", danced with both arms outstretched.

659He marked his whole body with tilaka and wore a kaupina;
devotion made him utterly humble and meek.

660Hearing of this, his wife
came running at once, weeping.

661Clasping Tirtha's feet she wept,
but Tirtharam paid no heed to her words.

662Her name was Kamala Kumari, and she was very beautiful;
her beauty lit up everything around.

663Tirtha took Kamala by the hand and said,
"I have given all my property to you.

664I have escaped from hell with my life;
you enjoy all the wealth and luxury."

665Hearing these words, Kamala Kumari
fell crashing to the ground.

666Seeing the net of maya that Kamala was casting,
Tirtharam smiled a little and said, "Chant the Name of Hari."

667Weeping, Kamala Kumari
went back home, and Tirtha became a beggar on the road.

668Having delivered Tirtharam, beautiful Gauranga
then left the holy place of Vateshvara.

[p. 62]

669How many people brought how many clothes!
But the Lord did not touch a single piece.

670At last the Lord called out "Govinda!"
and gave me a clap on the back:

671"We have spent seven days at this Vateshvara.
Let us go to Nandishvara to see him."

672Hearing this, I took the sandals on my shoulder
and, leaving Vateshvara, went with the Lord.

673On the way we came to a vast jungle,
and seeing it my heart failed me.

674That jungle stretched for ten kroshas,1
and I grew anxious: how would we get through?

675My all-knowing Lord smiled slightly
and went on ahead, while I fell behind.

676I followed the Lord along the footpath,
and by his will I felt no fear.

677How many beasts had their lairs there,
yet not one showed itself before or behind us!

678Having crossed the jungle, near the town of Munna
he sat beneath a tree to rest.

679Two householders of Munna came
and carefully brought some flour.

[p. 63]

680The Lord said nothing to them, good or bad,
and gradually the two sat down close by.

681Gazing at the young sannyasi, the two of them
looked at him fixedly, without blinking.

682Gradually towards evening a great hubbub arose:
the townspeople came in droves to see him.

683A fiery radiance flowed from the Lord's body,
and seeing it all the people stood stock-still.

684Gradually the people of Munna came forward
and one by one bowed down to him.

685With devotion all the people began to say,
"Come into the town, leave this tree."

686My Lord, absorbed in love, did not listen to their words;
inwardly saying "Hari", he was weeping all the while.

687Gradually feeling arose within him,
and at once the Lord got up and began to dance.

688Crying "Hari, Hari!", he falls to the ground,
and with him the village people grew excited.

689All of them, clapping their hands, began to dance,
and seeing this my Lord burst into tears.

690Any unbeliever who saw that state with his own eyes
felt devotion overflowing into his heart.

[p. 64]

691Thus half the night went by,
with all the people dancing and crying "Hari, Hari".

692At last the respectable married women, leaving their homes,
came to that place to see Gauranga.

693Having seen beautiful Gauranga with their own eyes,
the women could not go back home.

694Looking at one another, one said to the next,
"Seeing the sannyasi, my heart is in a turmoil.

695Sister, never have I seen anyone so handsome!
This is the one everybody calls Chaitanya Gosai.

696Ah, from fasting he is nothing but skin and bone!
Why at such an age has he bound up a load of matted hair?"

697Saying this, all the women of Munna
were overcome with weeping, tears flowing from their eyes.

698So the night passed, and no one slept.
In the morning my Lord rose and set off southwards.

699The people of Munna begged him in crowds to stay,
but my Lord would not listen to any entreaty.

700There was a very wretched woman there,
weeping beneath that tree, tears streaming from her eyes.

701When the Lord made ready to depart,
that old woman, weeping, begged for food and clothing.

[p. 65]

702She wore torn clothes and had no food in her belly.
Seeing her, Chaitanya Gosai stopped.

703Seeing her condition and understanding it in his heart,
the Lord, smiling a little, began begging alms all around.

704He said, "Give me alms, brothers of Munna;
when I have alms of food and clothing, then I shall go."

705The men and women of Munna, floating in joy,
brought heaps upon heaps of food and clothing.

706All said, "He wants provisions for the road,"
and so they brought them in heaps.

707Everyone was eager to put clothing into the Lord's hands,
and seeing the commotion the Lord began to laugh.

708All said, "Clothing is a trifle, worth nothing;
let Chaitanya Gosai take my cloth first!"

709No one knew what was in the Lord's mind,
and so they all hurried to bring food and clothing.

710The Lord said, "Listen, listen, people of Munna:
I have accepted your alms.

711Here beneath the tree sits this wretched woman;
give all this food and clothing to her."

712All the people were amazed at his compassion.
Someone said, "He begged alms for the old woman's sake."

[p. 66]

713Saying this, my Lord [adjusted] his outer cloth
and set off, saying "Hari, Hari".

714The Lord looked at me and made a sign,
and I followed behind with the water-pot and sandals.

715Many people began to walk along with him,
but the Lord did not once look back.

716One by one all the people turned back,
but Ramananda Svami would not leave him.

717Ramananda Svami is a man of great virtue;
privately I asked him what was in his heart.

718Ramananda said, "Brother, on seeing the Lord
my hard heart has melted.

719If the Lord does not make me his disciple,
I shall give up my life at once and not remain in the world."

720Then my Lord came to the town of Venkata,
arriving there at midday.

721There lived a learned gosai there,
a great Vedantic scholar without an equal.

722The foremost of pandits wanted to debate,
and the Lord replied, "I have lost."

723Even so the svami would not give up the debate,
and the Lord, his face beaming, began to laugh.

[p. 67]

724However much the svami argued for advaita-vada,
Chaitanya explained to him the doctrine of dvaita-advaita.2

725At last a fierce debate broke out,
and gradually the danda-svami admitted defeat.

726His name was Ramananda, and he was a great pandit;
Ramananda was initiated into the Name of Hari.

727The Lord poured the nectar of the Name into his ears,
and devotion overflowed in the svami's heart.

728Then Ramananda Svami bowed down
and at the Lord's command went back to his matha.

729The svami gave the Name of Hari to all his disciples,
and his mind grew drunk with the rasa of devotion.

730Staying three days in the town of Venkata,
the Lord gave the Name of Hari guilelessly from house to house.

731Men and women alike — all grew drunk,
and with them danced my Chaitanya Gosai.

732Town and villages, boys and girls grew drunk;
who could keep count of how many came and went?

733He gave everyone teachings on the truth of devotion,
and lifelong fools rolled at his feet.

734When the Lord saw an unbeliever, he would embrace him first,
and having embraced him, say to him, "Say 'Hari, Hari'."

[p. 68]

735There was a robber there named Pantha Bhil.
Hearing of him, the Lord went off towards him.

736Everyone said, "Holy man, do not go there!
What if Pantha Bhil kills you?

737Pantha Bhil is a villain with no sense at all;
finding you, he may do you some harm."

738Heeding no one's words, Chaitanya Gosai
hurried towards Bagula, to Pantha Bhil.

739Pantha Bhil lives in a forest called Bagula;
whenever he finds a traveller he brings him to ruin.

740Ignoring every warning, into the fearful forest
the Lord went, to see the sport.3

741I followed behind with the water-pot,
and Chaitanya Gosai said nothing to me.

742Finding the Lord, Pantha received him as a guest,
and Mahaprabhu stayed there three nights.

743The Lord said, "Pantha, you are a worthy holy man;
seeing you, all my sins are destroyed.

744You do not live in a house like a householder;
you are a supreme sadhu, a detached sannyasi.

745You are no worm of worldliness like a householder;
I see your heart is content with whatever comes.

[p. 69]

746You have no son, no daughter, no wife;
you are not drunk with worldly things and have no attachment.

747Blessed are you, King Pantha, crest-jewel of sadhus!
Seeing you, my heart has become glad.

748You regard worldly wealth as straw
and could give up all you have this very moment.

749You do not live with a woman —
that is why I came here, to fulfil my wish.

750You are always surrounded by disciples,
and on seeing you the heart thrills with joy.

751Noble one, you are not bound by maya and delusion;
I think you are the best of sadhus."4

752Silently hearing the Lord's words,
he bowed down at once with devotion.

753Hearing the Name of Hari from the Lord's lips again and again,
an ocean of devotion surged up in his heart.

754The Bhil fell rolling at the Lord's feet,
and the Lord embraced him and let him hear the Name.

755All the robbers, drunk with the Name of Hari,
turned that forest into a garden of joy.

756From that day Pantha put on the kaupina
and became the best of sadhus, mature in knowledge.

[p. 70]

757By the Lord's grace Pantha gave up his sinful deeds
and always went about dancing and chanting the Name of Hari.

758As soon as he took Hari's name, tears would come.
The young sannyasi was drunk with joy.

759All the robbers there were in the forest
gave up their wicked ways and together cried "Hari, Hari".

760All together they grew drunk with joy in that forest;
for the Lord's sake they all gave up their sinful deeds.

761Having thus purified Pantha Bhil,
my hero of dharma went on, floating in joy.

762His body wasted by fasting, he can hardly walk,
yet still the Lord gives the Name of Hari from house to house.

763The people of that country say "khai, mai",5
yet still Chaitanya Gosai distributes the Name.

764My Lord has no desires whatever,
yet wherever and whenever he goes, there is plenty of everything.

765Whoever sees the Lord even once
no longer has the strength to go away.

766Such is the Lord's power — what more can I say?
He has broken the dam of the ocean of devotion once again.

767Surging up, the ocean of devotion flooded the land;
some became sannyasis, some dervishes.

[p. 71]

768Some became detached Vaishnavas there,
some, turned aul and baul,6 dance in the courtyards.

769Thus my Lord, drunk with the Name,
rolls on the ground, lost in ecstasy.

770Sometimes he is like inert matter, with no outer awareness,
his body bristling like a kadamba flower.

771His eyes half-closed, like a corpse;
no one has ever seen such a wondrous state.

772Heedless of thorns and splinters, he falls to the ground;
think as I may, I cannot tell what mood he is in.

773Three nights passed beneath a tree;
he fasted and ate nothing.

774Tears streamed down over his breast;
call him a hundred times and not a word, like a madman.

775Sometimes he rolls on the ground, naked,
and I carefully take him up in my arms.

776On the fourth day a woman came
and showed hospitality, giving flour and parched grain.7

777Another old woman brought milk;
the Lord mixed the flour with the milk and made an offering.

778Three kroshas from there is a temple
where a linga called Girishvara was installed by the Creator.

[p. 72]

779People say that Vishvakarma built the temple
and the Grandsire8 worshipped Shiva with his own hands.

780There stands a huge bilva tree,
its branches spreading over a quarter of a krosha.

781I had heard that this tree bears no fruit;
going there, I saw that wonder for myself.

782On three sides the temple is surrounded by hills,
and on the south side the bilva tree stands in splendour.

783Gathering bilva leaves with his own hands, my Lord,
lost in love, offered them to Shiva by the handful.

784Then, drunk with love, Gora Raya
flailed about and fell crashing to the ground.

785Now laughing, now weeping, like a madman,
tears streaming unceasingly down his breast.

786His hair standing on end, almost inert;
the wondrous state of love is beyond words.

787The Lord has no desire; he is drunk with the Name of Hari.
Some two days passed in that abode of Shiva.

788On the third day a sannyasi with matted hair
came down from the mountain top and showed himself.

789That excellent sannyasi, keeping a vow of silence,
performed his worship and went back to the mountain top.

[p. 73]

790That solitary sannyasi had nothing on his body;
whoever sees him, even a worldly man becomes detached.

791When the Lord regained consciousness,
I told him everything about the sannyasi, one thing after another.

792Hearing about the sannyasi, my Gora Raya
hurried up the mountain to see him.

793I ran behind him in wonder,
and gradually we reached that place.

794Climbing the mountain, we saw
that sannyasi gosai beneath a tree.

795No cloth, no bowl — nothing beside him.
I stood behind Chaitanya.

796The excellent sannyasi, sunk in meditation, had no outer awareness;
whoever saw him became virtuous.

797However humbly Gora Raya spoke to him,
the sannyasi's meditation did not break.

798Then the Lord, with folded hands, began a hymn of praise,
and at that the excellent sannyasi began to look at him.

799Seeing the Lord, that sannyasi thakura
smiled, and great joy welled up in his heart.

800Who knows why the sannyasi smiled;
a moment later the Lord sat down beside him.

[p. 74]

801Two other detached sannyasis came there,
and the sannyasi wished to offer hospitality.

802He brought fruits called parata,
and the Lord took two of them.

803He gave me four fruits to eat.
"Unless it is prasada, I will not accept it," I said.

804Hearing this, my Lord Chaitanya Gosai
made the fruits into prasada and gave them to me.

805Parata fruits are very sweet, like nectar;
having eaten them, my mind grew restless.

806These sinful eyes of mine, out of greed,
kept glancing again and again at the Lord's fruits.

807Beautiful Gauranga smiled slightly
and held out two neem fruits9 to me.

808"How shall I eat these fruits?" I was afraid,
and at once I remembered the son of Anjana.10

809Seeing me hesitate and not eat the fruits,
Chaitanya Gosai said with a smile:

810"The stone won't stick in your throat, Govinda.
Don't play tricks when you are given prasada.

811Your desire to eat the fruit has grown strong,
but you are beside yourself for fear of a stone getting stuck."

[p. 75]

812When Gosai spoke out what was in my mind,
I at once put the fruit down and fell at his feet.

813In the end, at the Lord's order, I had to eat them,
and the sannyasi came and brought two more fruits.

814After eating, cupping my hands at the spring,
I drank water with a joyful heart.

815The cool, crystal-clear water of the spring —
drinking it, my whole body was refreshed.

816Drunk with the Name of Hari, the Lord was filled with love,
and his body bristled like a kadamba flower.

817In the surge of love the knot of his matted hair came loose,
his feet tangled together and he fell.

818His forehead was cut by a blow from a stone,
and streams of blood fell to the ground.

819Saliva flows from his mouth, water from his nose;
Gora Raya lies like a lifeless thing.

820Seeing this, devotion arose in the sannyasi;
he fell at the Lord's feet and began to weep.

821His body like a charred log, no cloth on his limbs;
his matted hair came loose and he breathed heavily.

822Tears streamed down through his beard,
and in love that charred log seemed to swell into blossom.

[p. 76]

823Then, regaining consciousness, my excellent Lord
rose and sat up, grey with dust.

824The excellent sannyasi was in a fever of agitation
and, gazing at the Lord, said, "You are God."

825At the sannyasi's words the Lord put his hands over his ears
and said again and again, "Sannyasi, give up such talk."

826The sannyasi said, "You are by no means a man."
The Lord said, "Sannyasi, you are my God.

827Wondrous is your love for God;
seeing you, even the unbeliever remembers him.

828No cloth, no bowl, no craving for wealth —
millions of obeisances to your feet.

829You are not subject to earthly pleasures;
beside you even heaven seems paltry."

830Then the Lord went to the town of Tripadi11
and, seeing the image of Sri Rama, fell in the dust.

831Many Ramat Vaishnavas12 live there,
and they go about every which way looking for debate.

832A Ramat pandit named Mathura
was known in the town as a great disputant.

833He came before the Lord and demanded a debate,
and the Lord, with folded hands and shrinking, replied:

[p. 77]

834"Mathura Thakura, I do not know how to debate;
a hundred times I admit defeat before you.

835You are a devotee of Sri Rama, a Vaishnava gosai;
by serving you, how many truths I shall learn!

836You are a detached Ramat, yet ruled by the lust for victory —
why smear soot with both hands over your spotless name?13

837Tell us something of the truth, so that, hearing it,
the people may be purified by your words.

838I hear you are very skilled in logic,
but there is no merit at all in dry logic.

839The truth of God, the truth of the soul, the doctrine of maya —
explain them and let us taste the nectar.

840Explain what makes living beings fulfilled,
and tell us that, worthy sir.

841There is no need for much debate and wrangling;
kindly tell me the subtle truth."

842As he was speaking, the Lord cried "Hari bol!"
and, growing excited, became drunk with the Name.

843Where was his cloth, where his upper wrap?
His hair standing on end, he breathed fast.

844Then he fell crashing to the ground
and lost consciousness, the Lord becoming almost inert.

[p. 78]

845All the Ramats, seeing that state,
surrounded the Lord and began to dance.

846Some said, "This sannyasi is no man";
some fell at his feet and rolled on the ground.

847After that he left the place,
and Mathura ran after him a long way.

848Smiling, he sent Mathuranatha away,
and the Lord hurried on to see Pana-Narasimha.14

849Lord Nrisimha is offered a sugar drink as bhoga,
and so everyone calls him Pana-Narasimha.

850The merciful Lord sang a hymn to Nrisimha,
and all the people were amazed to see it.

851Nrisimha's priest is Madhavendra Bhuiyan;15
every day he comes and worships Lord Nrisimha.

852He brought a tulasi garland and put it round the Lord's neck,
and wearing the garland, my Lord said "Hari, Hari".

853The pujari quickly brought some prasada,
and the Lord took just a particle in his hand.

854Holding the prasada in his hand, he sang its praises,
and as he took the prasada tears flowed from both his eyes.

855He had sugar drink brought for me,
and I drank and drank until my belly was full.

[p. 79]

856Nrisimha's drink is like nectar;
whoever sees Lord Nrisimha realises the state of Brahman.

857With closed eyes, the Lord says the Name of Hari;
gradually we arrived at the abode of Vishnukanchi.

858At Vishnukanchi a sheth16 named Bhavabhuti
serves Lakshmi-Narayana with great care.

859The sheth is a great devotee, a crest-jewel of saints;
his very life is given to Lakshmi-Narayana.

860Every day the worthy sheth serves with devotion
and spends much money on that service.

861His wife washes the temple every day;
that crest-jewel of saints is always busy with service.

862Every day sweet rice is made from two maunds of thickened milk,
and how many wandering ascetics go to receive the prasada!

863Seeing Lakshmi-Narayana, beautiful Gauranga
bowed down and sang long hymns of praise.

864Six kroshas from Lakshmi-Narayana
stands Shiva Trikaleshvara in the open plain.

865His gauripatta17 measures four cubits;
seeing that Shiva, the Lord was astonished.

866From there Pakshigiri18 can be seen;
below it is Pakshitirtha, where the river Bhadra flows.

[p. 80]

867Beautiful Gauranga bathed in that place
and ate the champi fruits that I obtained by begging.

868We lay down to sleep beneath a tree,
and in the night a tiger attacked us.

869Seeing its snarling and roaring, my Gora-chand
smiled and spread the snare of the Name of Hari.

870Hearing the cry of "Hari!", the tiger tucked in its tail
and with one bound retreated into the forest.

871Having seen this wondrous power with my own eyes,
I took up the dust of his feet and placed it on my head.

872Five kroshas from the bank of the Bhadra
is a holy place called Kalatirtha.

873There is an image of Lord Varaha of wondrous workmanship,
seeing which the sages and rishis are enchanted.

874Having had darshan, the Lord bowed down,
and a pujari with a happy face brought him a garland.

875Receiving the sanctified garland, the Lord was thrilled at heart;
his body began to tremble and his eyes to stream.

876The tears spurted out like a squirt-gun,
and, sobbing, the Lord was quite overcome.

877Five kroshas to the south is Sandhitirtha;19
the Lord set off, and I followed behind.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. A krosha (krosh) is a measure of distance of about 3–3.5 km.
  2. Dvaita-advaita, the doctrine of "unity in difference", as opposed to the strict monism (advaita-vada) of the Shankara school.
  3. "To see the sport": Govinda stresses Chaitanya's fearless playfulness.
  4. The whole speech is ironic: Chaitanya praises the robber for "virtues" that are really his vices (he has no family and is indifferent to others' property), and so disarms him.
  5. "Khai, mai" imitates an unfamiliar language (Telugu or Kannada) that a Bengali could not understand.
  6. Auls and bauls are Bengali wandering ecstatic singers and ascetics; Govinda applies to the South the categories familiar to him.
  7. Chuna: probably parched or crushed grain.
  8. The Grandsire (Pitamaha) is Brahma.
  9. Neem (nimba) is a bitter fruit; Govinda is apparently afraid of its hard stone.
  10. The son of Anjana is Hanuman, whom Govinda invokes in his fright.
  11. Tripadi is Tirupati.
  12. The Ramats (Ramanandis) are Vaishnavas who worship Rama.
  13. Literally, "why smear ink with both hands over your whiteness?"
  14. Pana-Narasimha is the Nrisimha temple at Mangalagiri (Andhra Pradesh), where the deity is offered the sweet drink pana.
  15. Bhuiyan (bhuñā) is probably a surname or a landholder's title.
  16. A sheth (shethi) is a merchant.
  17. The gauripatta is the base (yoni) of the Shiva-linga.
  18. Pakshigiri and Pakshitirtha are Tirukkalukundram, the "hill of birds" near Chengalpattu, famous for the legend that two eagles come there every day to be fed.
  19. The name is corrupt in the edition (sahita ghaṁ); probably the next tirtha listed in the index of the 1926 edition.
